mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Companies Registry / Trade Registry in the shareholder's state of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if shareholder's state is a contracting party to the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961); otherwise full Consular Legalization via the Luxembourg embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of residential address of each ultimate beneficial owner, director, and senior manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or competent administrative authority in the UBO's country of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, followed by notarised signature verification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing credit institution, with signature authenticated by a Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (where the bank letter requires public authentication)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial Power of Attorney granted by each shareholder to the Luxembourg notary and corporate service provider for incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and current register of directors and shareholders of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or authorized corporate services provider of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Executed charter or vessel-operator consent evidencing the ISIC 5222 offshore supply vessel leasing commercial purpose
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Counterparty charterer or vessel beneficial owner, notarised locally
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, with certified translation into French, German, or Luxembourgish

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs, and underlying charter counterparties against: (i) EU Council consolidated financial sanctions list; (ii) UN Security Council consolidated list; (iii) OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists; (iv) Luxembourg Cellule de Renseignements Financiers (CRF) circulars and CSSF warnings; (v) FATF high-risk jurisdiction lists. PEP identification follows FATF Recommendations 12 and 22, covering foreign and domestic PEPs, family members, and close associates; enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any PEP or sanctioned relationship. Screening must be repeated at least quarterly and upon each new transaction threshold and charter counterparty onboarding, with results retained in the statutory AML file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via www.lbr.lu; pre-incorporation name check and reservation executed electronically by the appointed Luxembourg notary through the eJustice / LBR e-filing system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name may be expressed in any Latin-script language; the legal form suffix 'SARL' or 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' is mandatory and non-negotiable. Non-Latin scripts are not admitted. French, German, Luxembourgish, or English names are preferred. All statutory filings (articles of association, RCS registration, RES publication) must be in French, German, or Luxembourgish; every foreign-language document in the notarisation bundle requires a certified translation into one of these languages.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: SCS (if inconsistent with the SARL legal form)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the notary or applicant for the RCS/LBR receives a written refusal notice. The applicant may file an administrative Request for Revision with the RCS through the appointed notary within 15 days of the refusal, annexing evidence of distinctiveness, prior use, or consent of the conflicting name holder. If the RCS upholds the refusal, an appeal lies to the Luxembourg Chamber of Commerce (Registre auxiliaire) within one month, and ultimately to the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement, commercial chamber) under Article 28 of the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS. A parallel fresh name application may be submitted at any time. A valid name reservation may be extended once for an additional 30 days upon proof that notarial deed execution is imminent.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Registered-office-only domiciliation through an approved regulated fiduciary (FCC/SOC) under the Law of 31 May 1999 is admissible for a SARL. However, for an offshore marine chartering entity (ISIC 5222), the Luxembourg tax administration (RIT) and AML obliged institutions expect real commercial substance, including local management decisions, accounting, bank accounts, and board meetings. A pure letterbox address with no operational activity exposes the company to tax-residency challenge, EU ATAD economic-substance review, and enhanced due diligence by Luxembourg credit institutions.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 50-70% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 24 months of operation, driven by the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier of offshore vessel chartering, the domiciliation agent's inspection duties under Article 5 of the Law of 31 May 1999, and CSSF AML supervision.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Title V, Articles 710-1 et seq. (Société à Responsabilité Limitée / SARL), as modernized by the Law of 23 June 2016, and the Law of 2 September 2011 on access to the professions for the commercial establishment authorization
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (Acte constitutif de la société à responsabilité limitée) executed before a Luxembourg notary, including the Articles of Association (Statuts) and the share subscription list
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum issued share capital of EUR 12,000, fully subscribed; cash contributions must be paid up to at least 25% of the nominal value of each share at incorporation, with the balance payable within five years; in-kind contributions must be fully paid up at constitution; the paid-up capital must be deposited in a Luxembourg blocking account and released only upon RCS registration
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the incorporators subscribe in full the minimum share capital of EUR 12,000, divided into 120 shares of EUR 100 each, and that all shares are allotted as recorded in the subscription list. RESOLVED that the registered office of the company be fixed at [street address], Luxembourg, and that the draft Articles of Association be adopted in final form. RESOLVED that [Full Name] be appointed sole Manager (Gérant) of the company, with full powers to open bank accounts, execute chartering contracts, and complete registration before the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register. RESOLVED FURTHER that the Manager be authorized to file the notarial incorporation deed, pay all registration and publication fees, and procure all ancillary licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Pre-Incorporation Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — name reservation via MyGuichet.lu and the RCS portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit one to three proposed corporate names to the RCS directly through MyGuichet.lu or through the instructing notary. The RCS verifies the names for identity or confusing similarity with existing registered names, protected trademarks, and contrary legal terms. Once a name is accepted, it is reserved for a period of 60 days pending completion of the notarial deed; the corporate name must include the abbreviation SARL or the full legal form Société à Responsabilité Limitée.
required_dossiers: Up to three proposed corporate names
Passport or national ID copies of the incorporators
Power of attorney for legal representative, if any
Optional trademark search certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the preferred name is rejected, the next proposed alternative name is substituted and a fresh reservation is filed; there is no administrative appeal for name refusal, so the name is promptly amended and resubmitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Deposit Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution, or EU credit institution with a Luxembourg establishment, selected by the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account in the name of the future company (SARL en formation). Deposit at least the fully subscribed minimum capital, or where partial payment of cash shares is used, at least 25% of the nominal value of each subscribed cash share, with the balance committed for calls within five years. Obtain from the bank a blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) addressed to the notary, confirming the deposit and the irrevocable blocking of funds for the benefit of the company until the RCS registration certificate is produced.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association delivered to the bank
Passports or IDs of all shareholders and the proposed manager
Source of funds evidence and bank reference
Completed bank KYC forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises KYC queries, submit supplementary source-of-wealth and business-plan documentation; if the bank refuses the account entirely, open the blocked account at an alternative Luxembourg credit institution and issue a new blocking certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaire) attached to the Chamber of Notaries (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All incorporators, or their duly empowered attorneys, appear personally before the notary. The notary verifies the blocking certificate, the authenticity of signatures, the legality of the articles of association, and the eligibility of the manager. The notary then reads and executes the acte constitutif, recording full subscription of the 120 shares, appointment of the manager, and adoption of the registered office address. The notary obtains the statutory supporting documents and delivers authenticated excerpts for subsequent registry filings.
required_dossiers: Final draft Articles of Association
Bank blocking certificate (attestation de blocage)
Passports or IDs of incorporators and manager
Criminal record extract (casier judiciaire) for each manager
Consent of the registered office owner (letter of address) or concluded lease deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues observations on any clause, the incorporators subscribe an acte rectificatif or approve a revised draft before re-execution; if a proposed manager is ineligible, the incorporators appoint a substitute manager qualified under Luxembourg law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), electronic e-justice filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of execution of the notarial deed, the notary files the incorporation application with the RCS electronically. The filing includes the notarial deed and mandatory particulars: corporate name, legal form SARL, registered office, share capital, subscribed and paid-up capital, and manager details. The statutory fee is paid online. Legal personality is acquired as from the date of RCS registration, upon which the LBR issues the registration extract (extrait du RCS).
required_dossiers: Authenticated notarial incorporation deed
Share subscription list signed by the incorporators
Statement of registered office address
Manager acceptance and identity documents
Proof of payment of the RCS fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS files a query (note des observations), the notary responds within one month with corrected particulars; if the deed contains a substantive defect, a notarial rectificatory act is recorded and the application is re-filed with the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Official Electronic Compendium (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA), under the authority of the Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCS registration, the LBR automatically publishes a concise legal notice containing the corporate name, legal form, registered office, share capital, subscription particulars, and manager details in the RESA. The company must verify the accuracy of the published notice and preserve a certified publication extract for bank, notarial, and foreign-filing purposes.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract (extrait du RCS)
Legal notice drafted by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published notice contains an incorrect particular, the company files a rectification request (corrigendum) with the LBR within 15 days, and the corrected notice is subsequently published in RESA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy — General Directorate for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (classes moyennes), application lodged through the Guichet unique one-stop shop (MyGuichet.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the establishment authorization application for the merchant activity of chartering and operational leasing of offshore platform support ships (ISIC 5222 / NACE 77.34). The applicant must demonstrate professional capacity through a diploma or relevant professional experience and exhibit good conduct. Once granted, the authorization must be displayed at the registered office and communicated to the tax and social security administrations.
required_dossiers: Extract from the RCS (immatriculation certificate)
Criminal record extract (casier judiciaire) of all managing persons
Evidence of professional qualification or professional experience
Copy of the lease deed for the registered office
Tax and social security compliance attestations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the authorization is refused, an administrative appeal may be lodged with the Minister of the Economy within three months of notification; alternatively, a new application is submitted with a certified dossier demonstrating professional capacity and good conduct.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes, ACD) for direct taxes; Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA, AEDT) for VAT; integrated e-government portal: myguichet.lu; Luxembourg Business Registers portal for RCS registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Luxembourg SARL is formed by notarial deed and registered with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS); the RCS matricule number serves as the statutory business identification number. For direct taxation, the ACD opens a corporate tax file and issues a direct tax TIN upon registration/incorporation notification; for non-resident entities with a Luxembourg permanent establishment, a direct tax registration application and appointment of a local tax representative must be filed. For VAT, the taxable person must submit a VAT registration application (electronically via myguichet.lu or on prescribed form 640) to the AEDT, attaching constitutional documents, proof of economic substance, and, where required, appointment of a VAT representative; AEDT issues the VAT identification number in the format LU + 8 digits. A foreign entity leasing offshore vessels may need a Luxembourg commercial licence (business permit) issued by the Ministry of the Economy if it maintains a fixed establishment or is deemed commercially active in Luxembourg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no check-the-box election; classification follows the legal form, and a SARL is a per se resident corporation subject to entity-level taxation. Available electivities of relevance include (i) VAT fiscal unity (single taxable person) for Luxembourg group members, (ii) small-business VAT exemption election where annual turnover is below EUR 30,000, (iii) tax consolidation under Article 164bis of the Income Tax Law (integration fiscale), and (iv) no elective hybrid-mismatch carve-outs; ATAD hybrid rules apply mandatorily.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 annual taxable turnover (Luxembourg small-enterprise exemption); non-established taxable persons are not eligible for this exemption and must register from the first euro where taxable supplies are made in Luxembourg; a resident SARL carrying on offshore vessel chartering will generally exceed the threshold or be subject to B2B displacement/reverse charge.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No general B2B e-invoicing mandate and no real-time tax clearance, API stamping or digital SAF-T submission regime is in force as of 1 January 2025. Mandatory e-invoicing applies only to B2G supplies via the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 channel. VAT returns, recapitulative statements and annual listings are filed electronically through myguichet.lu; accounting and export substantiation files must be retained in a form enabling SAF-T XML audit extraction by AEDT.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Luxembourg applies exemption with credit (0%) to the supply, chartering and operation of sea-going vessels used in commercial maritime navigation, including offshore support vessels serving non-EU installations, and to ancillary services for the direct needs of such vessels (VAT Directive art. 148). Zero-rating also applies to goods physically exported outside the EU evidenced by a customs export declaration. For B2B charter services to foreign taxable customers, the place of supply is the customer's jurisdiction, so the supply is outside Luxembourg VAT if the customer holds a valid VAT registration in another EU member state or represents a non-EU taxable person; the invoice must state the applicable place-of-supply rule and the customer's VAT number, and the operator must retain charter party, vessel registry and seaworthiness documentation, and operational voyage records demonstrating non-EU or commercial oceanic use. If the recipient is a non-taxable person, use-and-enjoyment or transport-related special rules may re-ground the supply in Luxembourg; accordingly, the exporter must confirm each transaction's place of supply before applying zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (electronic Single Administrative Document / EX-A form in Luxembourg customs system) evidencing exit of the vessel or goods from EU customs territory
Bill of lading or non-negotiable sea waybill evidencing the physical repositioning or offshore operational use of the vessel outside Luxembourg/EU customs territory
Inward remittance certificate (SWIFT MT103 or Luxembourg bank credit advice) evidencing receipt of the charter hire from the non-resident counterparty within the 180-day repatriation window
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT verifies export and offshore charter claims strictly; absence of the customs and remittance bundle results in retrospective zero-rating reversal, assessment of 17% Luxembourg VAT, default interest, and denial of input VAT recovery. Administrative penalties for fraudulent export zero-rating range from EUR 250 to EUR 250,000, up to 20% of the evaded tax may be imposed, and criminal tax fraud proceedings may impose imprisonment and asset confiscation; the ordinary five-year VAT audit period is extended to ten years in fraud cases, and directors or tax representatives who knowingly signed false declarations may be held jointly and severally liable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for bank licensing and AML/CFT supervision, and the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance for monetary and exchange rate policy. Luxembourg is a euro-area Member State, so exchange rate policy is vested in the Eurosystem/ECB for EUR-denominated operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full liberalization of both current and capital account transactions in accordance with the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. The euro is freely convertible; no general foreign-exchange approval is required for inbound equity injections, loan disbursements, charter-hire payments, profit repatriation, or trade settlements. Profit remittance restrictions are not imposed by exchange-control law; the practical hurdles are corporate-law solvency tests, the arm's length principle, substance requirements, and the 15% Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends (reduced to 0% under the parent-subsidiary directive where conditions are met; reduced under applicable tax treaties). Payments to non-cooperative or high-risk jurisdictions may be refused by banks under AML/CFT obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender rules, mandatory conversion ratios, repatriation timelines, or central bank settlement requirements in Luxembourg. Export/charter receipts may be retained in any currency. The BCL nevertheless requires resident credit institutions and, where applicable, direct resident reporters to submit balance-of-payments statistical declarations for cross-border flows exceeding EUR 12,500 per operation, and transaction-level reporting applies under ECB Regulation (EU) No 1844/2006 and BCL Circular 201210/L. The SARL should instruct banks to use correct purpose codes and maintain supporting invoices and charterparty contracts to satisfy BCL statistical reporting without triggering AML reviews.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Luxembourg-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) authorised by the CSSF under PSD2 and supervised by the CSSF are permissible payment-service providers for operational treasury, charter-hire collection, and supplier disbursements; they may generate fast onboarding, multi-currency IBANs, and API-driven clearing. Legal constraints: an EMI cannot hold deposits, extend credit, offer investment products, or provide FX derivative hedging; settlement balances must be safeguarded under national transposition of PSD2/EMD2. Offshore digital EMIs merely registered as 'electronic money agents' or 'payment facilitators' are not authorised to serve a Luxembourg SARL with actual settlement risk; the treasury lead should use only CSSF-authorised EMI/PSP or EEA passported EMIs and obtain a valid agent agreement, safeguarding account, and SCA-compliant interfaces.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg AML law does not categorically require every director to appear physically at the bank branch. However, under the law of 12 November 2004, as amended, the credit institution must identify and verify the identity of all directors, senior managers, and ultimate beneficial owners before establishing the business relationship. In practice, Luxembourg banks treat offshore vessel chartering as medium-risk enhanced: they require physical or genuine live-interview verification for at least one natural person with signing authority, and remote opening may be accepted only for non-resident directors through an existing banking relationship, appointed European agents, and digital identity verification using approved Luxembourg eID schemes. The responsible manager and at least one UBO should expect a physical or equivalent high-quality video verification interview. A Luxembourg notary, corporate-services firm, or legal counsel may facilitate, but the bank retains full AML discretion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore holding ownership structure with multiple jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised articles of association, RCS excerpt, up-to-date UBO and share register, group chart, organigramme, corporate accountability declarations, LEI codes, audited accounts or opening balance sheet, and explanation of the commercial purpose of intermediate holding vehicles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Vessel chartering to entities in sanctioned or high-risk waters or ambiguous charterparty counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full charterparty contract, vessel AIS records and voyage history, sanctions screening reports (EU, UN, OFAC, UK), safety management certificates (ISM), International Ship Security Certificate (ISPS), P&I insurance cover, commercial invoices, and a written trade-control policy confirming no sanctioned Russian, Belarusian, Iranian, North Korean, Syrian, Cuban, or Crimea transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value or high-frequency cross-border payments inconsistent with vessel leasing activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed invoice ledger, port call and delivery order documentation, MT103 transaction history, charter-hire schedules, vessel registration abstracts, flag state certificates, periodic BCL balance-of-payments reports, and narrative description of each payment class (bunkers, crew, port dues, repairs, insurance premiums).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection by non-resident shareholders or intercompany loans
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised share subscription deed, bank credit advice of subscription payment, shareholder loan agreement with commercial interest rate and maturity, source-of-funds evidence (bank statements, sale contracts, dividend records), transfer pricing analysis, Luxembourg substance documentation (registered office, board minutes, management appointments), and clean tax residence/beneficial ownership declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected receipts from third parties whose beneficial owners are undisclosed or opaque
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence file on charterers, ownership registry extract from the flag authority, commercial registry, source of charterer funds, invoice and payment schedules, sworn declarations, and legal opinion on ultimate beneficial owner identification under AML requirements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the initial share capital contribution in a Luxembourg SARL, use a wire transfer denominated in EUR to the bank account designated in the notarial deed, referencing the company name and 'Capital Subscription'. The bank will credit a temporary capital escrow/subscription account until registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS). From EU payment accounts, a SEPA Credit Transfer using IBAN and BIC is sufficient; from outside the EEA, use SWIFT MT103 with field 70 containing purpose code CAPC (Capital Payment) or an equivalent ISO 20022 code, and field 72 include the RCS reservation and notary reference. The originator must be the shareholder's own account; third-party payments are generally rejected. Cash, bearer instruments, and cryptocurrency are not acceptable for capital formation. For shareholder loans, use purpose code CTAX/INVS and an executed loan agreement; the bank may require evidence of beneficial ownership, source of funds, and payment of any applicable financial transaction taxes, although Luxembourg imposes no stamp duty on ordinary loan advances. Inbound funds from non-EU jurisdictions are subject to Regulation (EU) 2015/847 information requirements; the payment must show full originator and beneficiary identification, and the bank must report cross-border flows to the BCL for statistical purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for telegraphic transfers covering charter-hire remittances, insurance premiums, bunker settlements, port dues, crew payroll, and owner's disbursements. EUR payments inside the EEA clear via TARGET2 using MT103-equivalent ISO 20022 pain.001/pacs.008 with the beneficiary IBAN and purpose code TRAD or CHGS; USD payments clear through correspondent banks via SWIFT MT103 and may require MT202 COV for interbank settlement. For vessel acquisition or long-term lease capital expenditure, Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700/MT720) with payment at sight or deferred payment, backed by a conformity certificate, bill of lading, and marine insurance, is the preferred documentary clearing rail. The Luxembourg SARL should maintain segregated accounts for operational cash and escrowed/marine proceeds to preserve the integrity of the vessel leasing business and avoid mixing personal or non-trade flows. All outbound payments must include correct purpose codes, LEI where applicable, and supporting contract references to withstand BCL statistics and AML checks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or less liquid emerging-market currencies, booked with a licensed European bank permitted by EMIR and CSSF rules
Plain-vanilla FX options, subject to board treasury policy and EMIR clearing thresholds

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (Equity and Notes to the Financial Statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial year end + 6 months for shareholder approval; filing with RCS within 1 month after approval. Calendar-year SARL: approval by 30 June, filing by 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes responsible managers to fines up to EUR 25,000; two consecutive years of non-filing may trigger RCS administrative strike-off and dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 December of the calendar year following the tax year; mandatory e-filing via ACD electronic portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 10% late-payment penalty plus interest at 0.6% per month on unpaid tax; ACD may issue an estimated assessment and apply additional administrative fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net Wealth Tax Annual Return (Integrated with Form 100)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as corporate income tax return: due by 31 December of the year following the tax year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing results in the same penalty regime as corporate income tax, including monthly interest and estimated assessments; willful omission may lead to criminal fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO (Beneficial Owner) Register Update / Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) – administered by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 1 month of the event; no periodic annual UBO filing is required absent a change, but an annual internal verification at the general meeting is standard practice.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted UBO filing exposes the SARL and its managers to criminal fines ranging up to EUR 250,000 for ordinary breaches and up to EUR 1,250,000 for serious or repeated breaches.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for a SARL exceeding two of three thresholds for two consecutive fiscal years: balance sheet total > EUR 4.4 million; net turnover > EUR 8.8 million; average employees > 50. Audit is also compulsory for financial-sector licensees, securitisation vehicles, public interest entities, and upon demand of shareholders representing 10% of the share capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial accounts; IFRS is required for consolidated accounts of EU-listed companies and optional for individual statutory accounts of a SARL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg UBO law (Law of 13 January 2019) requires the RBE declaration to be kept in line with the SARL's actual beneficial ownership on an ongoing basis. Any shareholding transfer must be declared to the RBE within one month. Because the register is continuously updated, no separate annual confirmation is mandated, though an annual review coinciding with the shareholders' meeting is the accepted compliance safeguard.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors / Managers (Registre des Gérants)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500–5,500 per year depending on registered office and corporate agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000–15,000 per year for a typical non-listed SARL; higher if marine charter group consolidations are required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined headline rate in Luxembourg City (17% corporate income tax, 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT, and 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption (95% exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains), optional tonnage tax for qualifying shipping and offshore-supply vessel charter operations, 80% net-income exemption for qualifying IP income, and investment tax credit for eligible maritime assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 470 (Corporate Income Tax Return for legal entities) filed electronically via the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (ACD) e-Tax module on MyGuichet.lu
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end; e-filed returns are generally required where the ACD has provided the return form, and a provisional filing request can be accelerated to 30 June.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net profit before tax adjustments (résultat avant impôts) reconciling to the audited financial statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Luxembourg-source income only when filing as a non-resident taxpayer with a Luxembourg permanent establishment; attach tax treaty allocation schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable charter and lease revenue derived from offshore supply vessel operations under ISIC 5222
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use arm's-length charter rates; attach the transfer pricing local file and supporting voyage/employment documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating loss carryforwards utilized in the current tax year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filers may deduct only losses attributable to the Luxembourg permanent establishment and only within the statutory five-year restriction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Administrative fine of EUR 250 to EUR 2,500 for late filing, a 10% default-assessment increase on reconstructed taxable income, monthly late-payment interest of 0.6%, and criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 or imprisonment for deliberate false declarations.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Beneficial owner must obtain a Luxembourg/e-State Certificate of Tax Residence from the ACD, submit the certificate to the withholding agent before distribution, and, if tax was withheld, file an advance refund claim; the parent must provide a valid tax residence certificate and evidence of beneficial ownership within three years of the distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: No domestic withholding tax on outbound interest or royalties; the EU Interest & Royalties Directive and most DTAs provide 0%; a 20% anti-abuse levy may apply to payments to entities in non-cooperative or blacklisted jurisdictions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 500,000 of aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions triggers the Local File; preparation of a Master File is expected for groups with consolidated revenue above EUR 50,000,000; CbC reporting applies for groups with consolidated revenue above EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not maintain Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations, but central management and control, ATAD GAAR, and OECD BEPS Action 5 require the offshore-supply-vessel leasing entity to demonstrate commercial substance in Luxembourg through board decisions, operating control, qualified personnel, and real charter-management functions; inadequate substance will trigger income reallocation, denial of treaty benefits, and forfeiture of the participation exemption.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally understating charter income, fabricating offshore operation losses, or mischaracterizing lease receipts as non-taxable service fees
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; administrative penalty of 50% to 200% of the evaded tax plus 0.6% monthly late-payment interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax, subject to travel bans and up to 5 years imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Letterbox SARL with no personnel, no board meetings, no vessel-contract management, and de facto control exercised exclusively from a foreign parent jurisdiction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the corporate entity for tax purposes, reallocation of charter income to foreign shareholders, denial of treaty benefits, and a GAAR penalty of 10% of reclassified income (minimum EUR 5,000)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who permit the sham suffer piercing of the corporate veil, civil restitution for unpaid corporate taxes, judicial management prohibition, and travel bans

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging below-market bareboat charter rates to a group parent, paying unjustified management fees, or failing to produce an arm's-length benchmarking study for the offshore vessel lease
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACD upward income adjustment to arm's-length levels, denied deductions, 0.6% monthly late-payment interest, and administrative fines up to 10% of the adjustment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve non-arm's-length intercompany terms without documentation become personally liable for the underpaid tax; criminal liability for tax evasion if the pricing is wilfully fraudulent

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify the ultimate beneficial owner of the charter funds, omissions in the Luxembourg beneficial ownership register, and routing maritime charter payments through informal escrow providers to avoid AML scrutiny
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine up to EUR 5 million for the legal entity under Luxembourg AML law (Law of 25 March 2020), prohibition of activity, and civil fines for each aggravating deficiency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members and the AML responsible officer are personally liable for fines up to EUR 250,000, may face travel bans, and imprisonment up to 5 years for money-laundering or financing-terrorism offenses
